title: Bastion server catalog
description: The catalog Bastion ships as a starting point. It is not the list of servers a given install runs — that list lives in Application Support and the user edits it. Enforced by scripts/generate-servers.mjs before it writes anything.

id.description: Kebab-case. Becomes a URL path segment, a profile directory name and a JSON key.

transport.description: How Bastion reaches the server. `child` is an npm package run as a stdio subprocess; `remote` is an https endpoint somebody else operates, which Bastion installs nothing for and starts no process for.

distribution.description: npm means published, so Bastion can install it on demand; local means it resolves only against a checkout named by dev.json.

vendor.description: Who publishes the package. Stated rather than inferred from the scope, because the typo most worth catching is a typo IN the scope: `@mgcre/mcp-reddit` fails a startsWith check and would be waved through as somebody else's package. `mgcrea` holds the entry to the naming rule (@mgcrea/mcp-<id>, <id>-mcp, mcp-<id>); `third-party` requires a published package, derives localPath from the package name, and is what ServerDetail keys its provenance copy on — silence must not read as "ours".

url.description: The MCP endpoint. https only, and refused at runtime if it resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or metadata address — a URL here is the analogue of a command line, and the rule that nothing arriving over the wire can name one has to hold for URLs too.

dialect.description: The newest MCP protocol version the server itself speaks. Bastion translates to whatever each client asks for.

writeGate.description: Env var that gates destructive tools, or null when the server has no write path. Null is a claim that every tool is a read, not a shrug for a server Bastion cannot configure: ToolProbe turns it into "every tool is a read" and stops asking for confirmation.

writeGateSense.description: Which way the write gate points. `enables` (the default) means Bastion writes "1" for writes on; `disables` means the variable is a READ-ONLY switch and the values invert. Required on a third-party child that names a gate, because the convention is nobody's to assume: MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY, READONLY and ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS are all inverted, and the last one contains the word ALLOW, so no name heuristic can be trusted to tell.

gateBypass.description: Env vars that enable writes independently of the write gate. Bastion always forces these to "0"; they are never settable by a profile.

kind.description: Who obtains the credential. 'env' (the default) means the user fills the named variables. 'oauth' means Bastion runs an OAuth 2.1 flow and holds the token itself, so the mode names no variables at all; remote transports only. 'childOAuth' means the server logs itself in and keeps its own refresh token in its per-profile state, and Bastion only drives and reports that flow through the server's own tools; child transports only, and it names no variables either.

loginTool.description: childOAuth only. The server's own tool that performs the login. It opens a browser and blocks until its loopback callback lands.

statusTool.description: childOAuth only. The server's own tool reporting whether it is signed in. This is the only way Bastion knows: it never sees the token.

logoutTool.description: childOAuth only. The server's own tool that forgets the stored token.

stateEnv.description: Env vars naming on-disk state that must be redirected per profile.

format.description: A template over {port}. The path lives here rather than in Swift, for the same reason `Bearer` lives in env[].header.format rather than in a profile.

callbackEnv.description: Env vars naming a loopback OAuth callback URL. The first profile of a server is left alone so it keeps the default the server documents; a second profile gets an allocated port built from `format`, so two identities cannot race for one socket. Whatever is decided is kept, because the URL has to match an upstream app registration byte for byte.

secret.description: Kept in the Keychain and never written to a config file, never echoed in the Activity window.

boolean.description: Marks the variable a boolean, so the profile editor offers a choice rather than a text field. Every server that reads one parses it identically: 1/true/yes/on is true, any other non-empty value is false, and unset is NEITHER — it falls through to the server's own config file and then to the default below.

default.description: What the server does when this variable is unset. Not a value Bastion ever writes: it is the third state, and it is why a two-way toggle is the wrong control. It must match the server's own schema default — UNIFI_PROTECT_VERIFY_TLS defaults to TRUE, so an editor that assumed false and wrote "0" would silently stop verifying a console's certificate.

header.description: Remote transport only. The variable's sink: a request header rather than an environment variable on a child.

format.description: Template over {value}, so a profile holds the key rather than the word Bearer.

writeTools.description: Tool names the write gate hides, for a server with no writeGate to set: a remote endpoint, which has no environment at all, or a child whose own read-only switch is a CLI flag, which Bastion cannot pass. A filter over what Bastion forwards, never a promise about what the server will refuse. Mutually exclusive with writeGate — two switches on one wire drift apart.
